findings.title: The documented origin set omits the live function-write origin
findings.description: The page says only live and user are currently produced and that function is reserved and never matches. In the current realtime worker, a direct function's ctx.bounded mutation is authenticated with a dispatcher-minted capability containing the function name, and deriveWriteOrigin returns kind function with the function path and module. Live-invoked function writes instead preserve kind live. The page also conflates this data-plane write provenance with ctx.origin, which remains live-only or null inside the function body. This can make copied collection rules fail unexpectedly and understates that a rule such as @origin.kind != 'user' already admits direct function-originated writes today.
findings.recommendation: Document function as a current collection-rule origin and clearly separate function invocation auth provenance, downstream ctx.bounded write provenance, and the function body's ctx.origin value.

findings.title: The live actAs recipe cannot pass the deploy verifier
findings.description: The page presents function actAs as a live-call override and gives npcBrain an origin-only auth rule. The owning verifier requires every actAs function's auth expression to imply the app admin predicate. Live-call auth is evaluated before actAs under the null system principal, so an auth rule limited to @origin.kind == 'live' cannot imply an authenticated admin. The documented example is therefore rejected by bounded verify and deploy, making the advertised per-function live override unusable as shown.
findings.recommendation: Use session.live.runAs for the supported live service-identity pattern. Remove the origin-only actAs example unless the owning verifier is changed to safely recognize live-only actAs authorization.
